newsitem.title: USA: Top aide to former USDA chief Espy indicted in probe.
newsitem.headline: Top aide to former USDA chief Espy indicted in probe.

text.p: The top aide to former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy was indicted Tuesday on criminal charges of making false statements to federal investigators to conceal the receipt of almost $22,000 in outside consulting fees earned after he joined Espy's staff.

Independent Counsel Donald Smaltz announced that Ronald Blackley, chief of staff for Espy while he served on President Bill Clinton's cabinet, was charged with three separate false statement counts. The indictment marked the first criminal charges in the 2-1/2 year investigation of Espy against a member of his staff.

The indictment charges Blackley with "knowingly and willfully" making false statements in June of 1994 in a public disclosure report, and failing to report that he had received almost $22,000 from farmer clients of his for helping them obtain monetary subsidies from the Agriculture Department.
If found guilty of the charges, Blackley could be sentenced to up to five years in prison for each count and be fined a total of $750,000.
Espy has been under investigation since late 1994 for allegedly accepting illegal gifts and favors while he was agriculture secretary from companies his agency regulated.

The original allegations against Espy, a former congressman from Mississippi, stemmed from gifts he took from Arkansas-based Tyson Foods Inc., the nation's biggest poultry processor whose chairman Don Tyson has long enjoyed close ties with Clinton, former governor of Arkansas.
